title: Job Chapter 35 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 35 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 35 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 35.

questions.question: In Job 35, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?
Look unto the heavens, and see
If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him?
questions.explanation: The first event in Job 35 is Elihu speaking, as stated in Job 35:1.

questions.question: What did Job say about his righteousness?
options: My righteousness is more than God's
What advantage will it be unto thee?
Behold the clouds which are higher than thou
questions.correctAnswer: My righteousness is more than God's
questions.explanation: Job claimed that his righteousness was greater than God's, as referenced in Job 35:2.

questions.question: What question did Job ask regarding the profit of being cleansed from sin?
options: What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?
questions.correctAnswer: What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?
questions.explanation: Job questioned the advantage of being cleansed from sin, which is found in Job 35:3.

questions.question: Who will Elihu answer?
questions.explanation: Elihu states he will answer Job and his companions in Job 35:4.

questions.question: What does Elihu instruct Job to do in Job 35:5?
questions.explanation: Elihu instructs Job to look unto the heavens in Job 35:5.

questions.question: What does Elihu say about sinning in relation to God?
options: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him?
questions.correctAnswer: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him?
questions.explanation: Elihu questions the impact of sinning against God, as noted in Job 35:6.

questions.question: What does Elihu mean by saying to look at the clouds?
questions.explanation: Elihu directs Job to look at the clouds to recognize God's greatness, implied in Job 35:5.

questions.question: What were Elihu's companions doing?
questions.explanation: Elihu is addressing Job and his companions, implying they are listening, as stated in Job 35:4.

questions.question: What does Elihu ask about transgressions?
questions.explanation: Elihu questions what transgressions do to God in Job 35:6.

questions.question: Did Job claim that his righteousness is less than God's?
options: Only when he was in despair
questions.explanation: Job claimed his righteousness was more than God's, contradicting this statement in Job 35:2.

questions.question: Did Elihu express a concern about Job's view of righteousness?
questions.explanation: Elihu addresses Job's claim about righteousness, indicating concern in Job 35:2.

questions.question: Is it true that Elihu spoke to Job and his companions?
questions.explanation: Elihu specifically states he will answer Job and his companions in Job 35:4.

questions.question: Is it true that Elihu encouraged Job to look at the heavens?
questions.explanation: Elihu instructs Job to look unto the heavens in Job 35:5.

questions.question: Is it false that Elihu said Job should not worry about sin?
questions.explanation: Elihu actually addresses the issue of sin and its implications in Job 35:6.

questions.question: Is it false that Job asked what profit he would have if he sinned?
questions.explanation: Job asked about the profit of being cleansed from sin, not the act of sinning itself, as in Job 35:3.

medium.title: Job Chapter 35 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 35 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Job 35:7 ask regarding righteousness?
options: What do you give to God?
What do you lose when you sin?
What do you gain from prayer?
What do you teach the world?
questions.correctAnswer: What do you give to God?
questions.explanation: This is the essence of Job 35:7 which questions the value of human righteousness to God.

questions.question: What does Job 35:8 promise will happen if someone is righteous?
options: They will profit the son of man.
They will be free from all suffering.
questions.correctAnswer: They will profit the son of man.
questions.explanation: Job 35:8 indicates that righteousness may profit others, illustrating the communal impact of individual righteousness.

questions.question: According to Job 35:9, why do the oppressed cry out?
options: By reason of the arm of the mighty.
Due to their lack of wisdom.
questions.correctAnswer: By reason of the arm of the mighty.
questions.explanation: Job 35:9 explains that the oppression they face is what leads them to cry out for help.

questions.question: What does Job 35:10 suggest people should ask when in trouble?
questions.explanation: Job 35:10 highlights the need to seek God, especially in times of distress.

questions.question: According to Job 35:11, who teaches us more than the beasts?
questions.explanation: Job 35:11 states that God teaches us, implying divine wisdom surpasses that of animals.

questions.question: What does Job 35:12 indicate about the cries of the oppressed?
options: They go unanswered because of pride.
questions.correctAnswer: They go unanswered because of pride.
questions.explanation: Job 35:12 shows that the pride of evil men can prevent answers to the cries of the oppressed.

questions.question: What is the significance of Job 35:2 in the context of Job's claims?
options: It questions the validity of Job's argument.
questions.correctAnswer: It questions the validity of Job's argument.
questions.explanation: Job 35:2 challenges Job's claim that his righteousness is greater than God's.

questions.question: What does Job 35:6 imply about the effect of sin?
options: It does not affect God at all.
questions.correctAnswer: It does not affect God at all.
questions.explanation: Job 35:6 indicates that human sin does not change God's nature or affect Him directly.

questions.question: What is the call to action in Job 35:5?
questions.explanation: Job 35:5 encourages a focus on the divine and the greater context of creation.

questions.question: What does Job 35:4 suggest about Elihu's role?
questions.explanation: Job 35:4 shows Elihu's intent to provide answers and wisdom to Job and his companions.

questions.question: According to Job 35:3, what does Job question about his sin?
options: Its ability to bring him joy.
questions.explanation: Job 35:3 reveals Job's questioning of what advantage or profit there is in being cleansed from sin.

questions.question: What does Job 35:10 imply about the nature of God?
options: He is distant from human suffering.
He is a source of comfort.
questions.correctAnswer: He is a source of comfort.
questions.explanation: Job 35:10 emphasizes that God gives 'songs in the night', indicating His role as a source of comfort and hope.

questions.question: Job 35:12 indicates that the cries of the oppressed go unanswered due to what?
questions.explanation: Job 35:12 states that none gives answer because of the pride of evil men, indicating a reason for unanswered cries.

questions.question: According to Job 35:9, the mighty are the only ones who can help the oppressed.
questions.explanation: Job 35:9 suggests that the oppressors contribute to the cries of the oppressed, not that they can help them.

questions.question: Job 35:11 implies that humans can learn from animals.
questions.explanation: Job 35:11 clearly states that God teaches us more than the beasts, suggesting a higher level of wisdom given to humans.

hard.title: Job Chapter 35 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 35.

questions.question: According to Job 35:13, how does God regard vanity?
questions.explanation: Job 35:13 explicitly states, 'Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it,' indicating that God does not listen to or regard vanity.

questions.question: What does Job 35:14 advise about trusting God despite not seeing Him?
questions.explanation: Job 35:14 says, 'Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him,' encouraging trust in God even without visible proof.

questions.question: In Job 35:15, what is said about God's visitation and Job's awareness of it?
options: God hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity
God hath visited in mercy; and he knows it fully
God hath not visited at all
God's visitation is always clear to Job
questions.correctAnswer: God hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity
questions.explanation: Job 35:15 states, 'But now, because it is not so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth it not in great extremity,' showing that God's anger visitation may occur without Job fully realizing the severity.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Job 35:16 for Job opening his mouth in vain?
questions.explanation: Job 35:16 says, 'Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge,' indicating that Job speaks excessively without understanding.

questions.question: Which phrase from Job 35:13 emphasizes God's attitude towards empty or meaningless speech?
questions.explanation: Job 35:13 states, 'Surely God will not hear vanity,' emphasizing that God disregards empty or meaningless speech.

questions.question: What does Job 35:14 say is before God, even though man may not see Him?
questions.explanation: Job 35:14 mentions, 'yet judgment is before him,' indicating that judgment is always before God despite man's inability to see Him.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'hebel' (הֶבֶל) in Job 35:13 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'hebel' (הֶבֶל), used in Job 35:13 translated as 'vanity,' means emptiness or futility in scholarly Hebrew lexicons.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Job 35:16 where Job is described as opening his mouth in vain and multiplying words without knowledge?
questions.explanation: Job 35:16 uses irony, as Job’s attempt to defend himself results in vain and ignorant speech, highlighting the futility of his words.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God not listening to empty words as in Job 35:13?
questions.explanation: Psalm 115:1 states, 'Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory,' emphasizing that God does not respond to vain or empty praises, connecting with Job 35:13.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the principle of trusting God's judgment despite not seeing Him, similar to Job 35:14?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:1 defines faith as 'the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen,' paralleling the trust in God's judgment in Job 35:14.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Job 35:13 in the chapter?
options: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men
Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou
If thou be righteous, what givest thou him?
Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than God's?
questions.correctAnswer: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men
questions.explanation: Job 35:12, 'There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men,' precedes Job 35:13 directly.

questions.question: How does Job 35:8 contrast the effects of wickedness and righteousness?
options: Wickedness may hurt a man; righteousness may profit the son of man
Wickedness brings blessings; righteousness brings suffering
Wickedness is ignored; righteousness is punished
Wickedness and righteousness have equal effects
questions.correctAnswer: Wickedness may hurt a man; righteousness may profit the son of man
questions.explanation: Job 35:8 contrasts the consequences: 'Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; and thy righteousness may profit the son of man,' showing moral effects on others.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage similarly teaches that God is not moved by human sin or righteousness to receive gifts, reflecting Job 35:6-7?
questions.explanation: Psalm 50:9-12 declares that God does not need sacrifices from humans, paralleling Job 35:6-7 where human sin or righteousness does not give or receive anything from God.

questions.question: What is the cultural significance of the phrase 'who giveth songs in the night' found in Job 35:10, in the context of ancient Near Eastern literature?
options: It signifies divine comfort during suffering
It refers to literal night-time music festivals
It symbolizes human joy apart from God
It indicates darkness as God's punishment
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies divine comfort during suffering
questions.explanation: Job 35:10's phrase 'who giveth songs in the night' metaphorically represents God's comfort in times of distress, a common theme in ancient Near Eastern texts where night symbolizes hardship.

questions.question: True or False: Job 35:15 states that God visits in anger and Job fully understands the extremity of this visitation.
questions.explanation: Job 35:15 says God hath visited in anger, 'yet he knoweth it not in great extremity,' indicating Job does not fully understand the severity.

theological.title: Job Chapter 35 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 35 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 35:2 teach about human sin and righteousness?
options: It is wrongful for man to claim his righteousness exceeds God's
God's righteousness is inferior to human righteousness
Human righteousness is irrelevant before God
questions.correctAnswer: It is wrongful for man to claim his righteousness exceeds God's
questions.explanation: Job 35:2 explicitly challenges the claim that 'My righteousness is more than God's,' indicating it is incorrect to think human righteousness is superior to God's.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's response to human sin does Job 35:6 teach?
options: God is directly harmed by human sin
Human sin affects only other humans, not God
Human sin accumulates to change God's nature
God rewards sin with immediate punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin affects only other humans, not God
questions.explanation: Job 35:6 asks rhetorically, 'If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him?' indicating human sin does not cause direct harm to God himself.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the efficacy of human righteousness does Job 35:8 teach?
options: Human wickedness has no impact on others
Human righteousness benefits fellow humans, not God
Only divine righteousness has any effect
questions.correctAnswer: Human righteousness benefits fellow humans, not God
questions.explanation: Job 35:8 states, 'thy righteousness may profit the son of man,' showing that human righteousness benefits others rather than God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 35:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 speaks of God as 'my maker, who giveth songs in the night,' showing God's providential care and sustenance even in darkness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 35:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Job 35:13 says 'Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it,' indicating God's righteous anger and judgment against evil.

questions.question: How does Job 35:5 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine transcendence?
options: It shows God is subject to human limitations
It denies God's existence in the heavens
It portrays the heavens and clouds as higher than man, emphasizing God's exalted nature
It teaches that humans can reach God by their own effort
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays the heavens and clouds as higher than man, emphasizing God's exalted nature
questions.explanation: Job 35:5 invites looking to the heavens and clouds 'which are higher than thou,' highlighting God's transcendence above humanity, a theme consistent with Isaiah 55:9.

questions.question: How does Job 35:11 relate to the biblical motif of God as the source of wisdom?
options: It claims animals are wiser than humans
It denies any special wisdom given by God
It teaches God imparts wisdom above that of beasts and birds
It states humans gain wisdom only through experience
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches God imparts wisdom above that of beasts and birds
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says God 'teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth,' affirming God as the giver of superior human wisdom, a theme found also in Proverbs 2:6.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 35:6 and Job 35:7 teach about human actions and their effect on God?
options: Human sin and righteousness change God's nature
Human actions neither harm nor benefit God
Sin causes God to punish others immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Human actions neither harm nor benefit God
questions.explanation: Job 35:6 and 35:7 together ask what human sin or righteousness gives or does to God, concluding that human actions do not affect God directly.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 35:12 and Job 35:13 teach about God's response to human speech and pride?
options: God listens attentively to all human complaints
Prideful and evil speech is ignored by God
God rewards prideful speech with blessing
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: Prideful and evil speech is ignored by God
questions.explanation: Job 35:12 and 13 say that cries go unanswered because of the pride of evil men and that God does not regard vanity, showing He rejects proud, empty speech.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 35:14 and Job 35:15 teach about divine judgment and human trust?
options: Judgment is hidden and unknown to God
God's judgment is present and humans should trust despite apparent absence
Humans should distrust God because He does not judge
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is present and humans should trust despite apparent absence
questions.explanation: Verse 14 commands trust because judgment is before God, while verse 15 notes God's anger visits even if humans do not perceive it fully, affirming divine justice and trustworthiness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Job 35:9-12 imply God ignores the cries of the oppressed due to prideful evil men. What does Job 35:9-12 actually teach?
options: God actively helps the oppressed without exception
Cries go unanswered because God is absent
The cries arise because of oppression, but God’s silence is related to human pride, not divine neglect
God punishes the oppressed for their pride
questions.correctAnswer: The cries arise because of oppression, but God’s silence is related to human pride, not divine neglect
questions.explanation: Job 35:9-12 explain that the oppressed cry out due to the arm of the mighty, but no one asks 'Where is God my maker?' and answers are withheld because of the pride of evil men, not because God neglects them.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s knowledge and human limitation does Job 35:16 teach?
options: Humans can fully understand God's ways
Job speaks with full divine knowledge
Job’s words are vain and show lack of knowledge
God is ignorant of human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Job’s words are vain and show lack of knowledge
questions.explanation: Verse 16 states that Job 'multiplieth words without knowledge,' indicating Job’s speech is futile and lacking true understanding compared to God's wisdom.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Job 35:1 by Elihu’s speech introduction?
questions.explanation: Elihu begins speaking with a doctrinal correction to Job, demonstrating God’s wisdom being revealed through him to correct misunderstanding, reflecting divine wisdom.

questions.question: What narrative arc does Job 35:4, where Elihu promises to answer Job and his companions, prepare for in Scripture?
options: The coming of the Law through Moses
The eventual divine response that reveals God's justice and wisdom
The establishment of the Davidic kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The eventual divine response that reveals God's justice and wisdom
questions.explanation: Verse 4 sets up Elihu’s role to respond to Job’s complaints, preparing for God’s own speeches that reveal divine justice and wisdom, a key theme in Job and broader Scripture.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about human sin and divine justice do Job 35:15 and Job 35:13 teach?
options: God ignores human sin in His judgment
God visits in anger but does not overlook human sin, demonstrating His righteous justice
Human sin causes God to lose control
questions.correctAnswer: God visits in anger but does not overlook human sin, demonstrating His righteous justice
questions.explanation: Job 35:15 mentions God visiting in anger, and 35:13 states God will not hear vanity, together affirming God's righteous judgment on sin.
